**Question 2.** What distinct energy-use profiles exist among Chicago's large buildings?

This document clusters buildings with k-means, using the cleaned data from Part 1 (render
`01_data_preparation_eda.Rmd` first). The Python version is `python/03_q2_clustering.ipynb`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)

bldg <- read.csv("../data/processed/buildings_latest_r.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(bldg)
```

# 1. Approach

As in Python: five standardized features (log site EUI, log GHG intensity, and the electricity, natural
gas and district-energy shares of site energy); k-means with 25 random starts; *k* chosen from the elbow
in the within-cluster sum of squares and the average silhouette width for *k* = 2 to 8. The ENERGY STAR
score is used only to describe the clusters, because it is missing for some buildings.

```{r choose-k}
features <- c("log_site_eui", "log_ghg_intensity", "elec_share", "gas_share", "district_share")
X <- scale(bldg[features])
d <- dist(X)

set.seed(42)
scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2:8, function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(X, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
  data.frame(k = k, within_ss = km$tot.withinss,
             silhouette = mean(silhouette(km$cluster, d)[, "sil_width"]))
}))

scores %>%
  pivot_longer(-k, names_to = "measure") %>%
  mutate(measure = recode(measure, within_ss = "Within-cluster sum of squares",
                          silhouette = "Average silhouette width")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(k, value)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Choosing the Number of Clusters", x = "Number of clusters k", y = "Value")
scores %>% mutate(across(-k, ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

**Interpretation.** The silhouette is highest at k = 2 and 3
(`r round(scores$silhouette[scores$k == 2], 3)` and `r round(scores$silhouette[scores$k == 3], 3)`) and
`r round(scores$silhouette[scores$k == 4], 3)` at k = 4, where the elbow bends. As in Python, k = 4 is
chosen because it separates the district-energy buildings as their own profile.

# 2. The clusters

```{r clusters}
set.seed(42)
km <- kmeans(X, centers = 4, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)
bldg$cluster <- km$cluster

# Name clusters from their average profile, as in Python
prof <- bldg %>% group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(site_eui = mean(site_eui), elec_share = mean(elec_share),
            district_share = mean(district_share))
names_map <- c()
left <- prof$cluster
for (rule in list(c("district_share", "District-energy buildings"),
                  c("elec_share", "Electric-led, low energy use"),
                  c("site_eui", "Energy-intensive, poor performers"))) {
  sub <- prof[prof$cluster %in% left, ]
  pick <- sub$cluster[which.max(sub[[rule[1]]])]
  names_map[as.character(pick)] <- rule[2]
  left <- setdiff(left, pick)
}
names_map[as.character(left)] <- "Gas-heated, typical"
bldg$profile <- unname(names_map[as.character(bldg$cluster)])

profile <- bldg %>% group_by(profile) %>%
  summarise(buildings = n(), median_site_eui = median(site_eui), median_ghg = median(ghg_intensity),
            elec_share = mean(elec_share), gas_share = mean(gas_share),
            district_share = mean(district_share),
            median_energy_star = median(energy_star, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_age = median(building_age), total_ghg_kt = sum(ghg_total) / 1000) %>%
  mutate(share_of_total_ghg = total_ghg_kt / sum(total_ghg_kt)) %>%
  arrange(median_ghg)
profile %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

```{r pca, fig.height = 5.5}
pcs <- prcomp(X)
ggplot(data.frame(PC1 = pcs$x[, 1], PC2 = pcs$x[, 2], profile = bldg$profile),
       aes(PC1, PC2, colour = profile)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "k-means Clusters (k = 4) on the First Two Principal Components",
       x = "First principal component", y = "Second principal component", colour = "Profile")
```

```{r composition, fig.width = 10}
comp <- bldg %>% count(profile, property_group) %>% group_by(profile) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))
profile_order <- profile$profile
ggplot(comp, aes(property_group, factor(profile, levels = profile_order), fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = round(pct))) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Property-Group Composition of Each Cluster (% of buildings in the cluster)",
       x = "Property group", y = "Energy profile", fill = "% of cluster") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r save}
write.csv(profile, "../report/figures/q2_cluster_profiles_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 3. Discussion

```{r get-values, include = FALSE}
p <- function(name, col) profile[[col]][profile$profile == name]
```

R finds the same four profiles as Python:

- **Gas-heated, typical** (`r p("Gas-heated, typical", "buildings")` buildings): mostly gas
  (`r round(100 * p("Gas-heated, typical", "gas_share"))`%), lowest GHG intensity
  (`r p("Gas-heated, typical", "median_ghg")` kg/sq ft).
- **Electric-led, low energy use** (`r p("Electric-led, low energy use", "buildings")`): lowest energy use
  but higher GHG intensity (`r p("Electric-led, low energy use", "median_ghg")`) than the gas-heated
  group, because grid electricity carries more CO2 per unit.
- **Energy-intensive, poor performers** (`r p("Energy-intensive, poor performers", "buildings")`): median
  ENERGY STAR score `r p("Energy-intensive, poor performers", "median_energy_star")`, producing
  `r round(100 * p("Energy-intensive, poor performers", "share_of_total_ghg"))`% of total emissions.
- **District-energy buildings** (`r p("District-energy buildings", "buildings")`): mostly district steam
  and chilled water, the highest GHG intensity
  (`r p("District-energy buildings", "median_ghg")`).

Cluster sizes can differ by a few buildings from Python because k-means' random starts differ between the
two languages, but the profiles and their decarbonization implications are the same: retrofit the
energy-intensive group first, electrify the gas-heated group, and rely on grid and district-plant
decarbonization for the other two.
